subject: Post-call recap: Ridgeback POC model slate + eval links
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Huang <claire@ridgeback.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-14T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: Ridgeback POC model slate + eval links

Thanks again for taking the call today — quick recap and next steps from our side. Short version: we think a 2–3 model POC will cover Ridgeback's tradeoffs and let us validate hallucination risk and latency under your traffic.

Recap (key asks you mentioned):
- Primary workload: product description generation + short Q&A in the UI (avg prompt ~60 tokens).
- Target SLO: 90% of replies < 250ms server-side p50, p95 < 800ms (you noted 95th is more important for UX).
- Failure modes: hallucinations on new SKUs and sensitive pricing language.

Recommended 3-model slate for POC (initial shortlist + rationale):
1) rw-lite-1.3b-int8 (cost-focused) — pros: ~3x cheaper in per-token execution, best for high-throughput catalog generation; cons: lower factual consistency on edge cases.
2) rw-balanced-3b-q4_0 (balance of quality/latency) — pros: solid quality/latency tradeoff; good baseline for UI responses; cons: ~2x cost vs rw-lite.
3) open-7b-optim (high-quality fallback) — pros: highest factuality on product copy, good for critical pages; cons: higher latency and cost; suggest use as fallback for prompts flagged by classifier.

What we attached/linked for your review:
- ridgeback_prompt_set_v1.json (attached): the set of ~25 test prompts we captured on the call — please review and mark high-priority cases.
- ridgeback_benchmarks_summary.pdf (attached): our initial simulated latency/cost estimates (p50/p95) using your avg token lengths.
- Drive folder with raw bench data and prompt runners: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3benchmarks

Quality regression concerns and mitigation plan:
- We'll run baseline evals using your flagged prompts + our automated hallucination checks (entity hallucination and numeric drift).
- Canary policy: start 5% traffic to rw-balanced, monitor hallucination rate, token efficiency, latency p95. If hallucination > threshold, fallback to open-7b-optim while we gather fine-tune/rewrites.

Next steps (ask of Claire/Tom):
- Confirm which 6 prompts you want in the first round (I attached a suggested subset in the prompt file).
- Procurement: a quick ballpark for monthly committed tokens helps us size Dedicated vs Hosted — Tom, can you share your expected monthly token volume?
- We can run the first bench with your prompt set tomorrow if you sign off; would you prefer PST morning or early afternoon?

Thanks — copying Karthik and Aditya to schedule the bench runs and provide cost/latency detail.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
From: Claire Huang <claire@ridgeback.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-14T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Ridgeback POC model slate + eval links

Thanks Vanessa — that summary is helpful. A few quick notes:

1) I've looped Tom (procurement) on this thread (he's on cc). We expect ~120M generated tokens / month initially (catalog cycles + UI usage). Happy to refine.
2) SLO clarification: the UX team wants p95 under 700ms if possible; p50 target is fine.
3) Hallucination risk: our main worry is pricing and spec drift when models invent SKU attributes. We can provide a small canonical product table for grounding during tests.

Action items for your team: can you provide a very short cost estimate (hosted) for the three models above (per-1M-token) and an expected p95 on a standard nvidia a10g or equivalent? That will help procurement.

Also — happy to prioritize 8 prompts for the first round. I'll review the attached prompt file and send the picks by EOD.

Claire Huang
Head of Product, Ridgeback AI
claire@ridgeback.ai
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-14T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap: Ridgeback POC model slate + eval links

Aditya / Karthik — forwarding Claire's reply (and Tom on cc). She confirmed ~120M tokens/month and tightened p95 target to 700ms.

Can you run the following tomorrow:
- Bench the three models against ridgeback_prompt_set_v1.json (attached) and return p50/p95 latencies (server-side), and a hosted per-1M-token cost estimate we can share with procurement.
- Run hallucination checks on the 8 prompts Claire will pick (assume worst-case if she misses any).
- Recommend quantization/profile per-model that meets their p95 target on A10G-class hardware.

Proposed canary mapping (suggestion):
- 70% rw-balanced-3b-q4_0 (main)
- 25% rw-lite-1.3b-int8 (bulk catalog jobs; lower cost)
- 5% open-7b-optim (fallback for high-confidence-critical flows)

If we can get numbers by 4pm PST tomorrow, I'll send them to Claire and Tom with a proposed 2-week POC schedule.

Thanks — V

Vanessa / Aditya — quick bench summary and attachments (raw CSV attached). Will follow up with a short doc with charts tomorrow morning.

Summary (test environment: A10G-like instance, batch sizes tuned to 32 where applicable):
- rw-lite-1.3b-int8:
  - p50: 95ms
  - p95: 420ms
  - est hosted cost: $55 per 1M input+output tokens
  - notes: very cost-efficient, higher hallucination rate on entity-heavy prompts (observed 8% on our synthetic SKU tests).

- rw-balanced-3b-q4_0:
  - p50: 140ms
  - p95: 610ms
  - est hosted cost: $120 per 1M tokens
  - notes: best tradeoff; p95 sits under Claire's 700ms target in our runs when batch sizing is tuned. Hallucination observed ~3% on the SKU set.

- open-7b-optim:
  - p50: 320ms
  - p95: 980ms (higher than target)
  - est hosted cost: $420 per 1M tokens
  - notes: highest factuality (hallucination ~1%), recommend this as fallback for critical flows; to meet p95 target we'd advise an edge routing/fallback plan rather than making it primary.

Recommended quantization/profiles:
- rw-lite-1.3b-int8: use int8 runtime profile (recommended) — biggest cost savings with acceptable latency.
- rw-balanced-3b-q4_0: q4_0 profile tuned for A10G gives balanced latency.
- open-7b-optim: if latency <700ms is required, need larger GPU (e.g., H100) or use as fallback only.

Canary suggestion: start with 5% traffic to open-7b-optim (monitor hallucination + latency); scale main traffic to rw-balanced-3b once both hallucination and p95 stability are confirmed.

Attachments (sent):
- ridgeback_benchmark_results_v1.csv (raw latency traces and batch configs)
- ridgeback_cost_estimate_v1.xlsx (per-1M-token cost math and assumptions)
- ridgeback_prompt_set_v1.json (copy used for bench)

I'll prepare a 1-page executive summary for Claire with a short recommendation and sample canary timeline to send by 9am PST tomorrow.

—
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
